I like this game, I really do. I definitely think it lives up to its namesake and does a fantastic job of carrying on the franchise, namely the Kyle Crane saga. But real talk, there's definitely a level of challenge and difficulty here I wasn't expecting. I personally like that, but I can definitely see many gamers getting too frustrated with some of the lengthy requirement for some missions, and achievements for that matter. The one mission that comes to mind is the asylum mission (I'm not going to give too many details here, just an idea of how lengthy this is). First you go to the asylum, you do some things, then you need to escape, then meet up with your peeps after you did those things, then you need to quickly head over to the town hall to stop the Baron's men from doing the douchey things they typically do throughout the game (timed), then you need to go to 3 separate locations throughout town to once again stop the Baron's men from doing more douchey things (also timed), then you need to quickly head back to the town hall and do more things followed by a fight with chimera...sweet heavenly baby Jesus, that's a whole bunch of stuff for just one mission!!! 

Nightmare difficulty was just as the name implies, an absolute nightmare at times. Spending nearly the entirety of the game essentially getting one-shotted by the chimera and most of the Baron's men wasn't too fun. And no joke, those chimera fights honestly made me feel like I was playing that Resident Evil 7 DLC, the one with Jack's brother where you need to kill the absolute s*** out of everything with your fists. Then there was the overly grabby/feely regular infected that rarely give you more than 2 seconds to search a dead body because they perpetually seem to pop out of nowhere to 'cop more feels' off of you. Normally, that's not too bad, and pretty much what you'd expect, but on the highest difficulty it typically means you're either dying or dead before you even know what's happening.  By the end of the game I was yelling obscenities in such profusion that I'm pretty sure my soul is now eternally damned to hell, but it was worth it! 

 And then there's the Restored Land/One Life mode...oh boy! Definitely easier than many permadeath modes in a lot of games, but the lengthy setup to complete it, and the constant fear/stress that you could potentially screw something up easily and get killed really far into a run (spoiler alter: I did...a lot!) nearly broke me...but also worth it!

To sum up, I enjoyed my time with this game, I'll probably keep going back to it, and I think any fan of the series should give it a try.

This is going to be a long review focusing mostly on areas where the game can be improved. Everything else—like the music, atmosphere, sound design, art direction, and gore—is already perfect or close to perfection. With a few tweaks, this game could easily go from an 8/10 to a 9 or even a 10/10, completely surpassing the original.

The parkour is a more simplified version of the system in Dying Light 2. For me, it is a bit too clunky right now because of certain moves—specifically, I think the high jump should just be removed entirely. There is a setting to lower the jump height, which definitely makes it more immersive, and i love dl1 parkour so much because of its immersion from simplicity. I also find myself accidentally climbing things way too often when I don't want to. If they removed the high jump and the sprint run, the parkour would still be technical without feeling clunky.

When it comes to combat, the actual ragdoll physics are honestly better and are more than Dying Light 1. The main issue is just that ragdolls happened way more often in the first game. For example, when you throw a propane tank at a zombie, it just plays a stumbling animation, whereas in DL1 they would go straight into a full ragdoll. On a side note, I feel like zombies in dl1 produced more blood with this sort of blood mist effect.I wish dying light the beast zombies when hit would also produce this blood mist.

The basic combat flow is similar across both games: you hit an enemy a few times and then they go into a ragdoll state. Generally speaking, the hit animations in DLTB are amazing (using fist weapons is incredibly immersive). However, one really annoying feature in DLTB is getting stunned whenever a regular zombie hits you. I'm pretty sure that didn't happen in DL1, which allowed you to keep slashing through groups uninterrupted.

Overall, the content itself is amazing, and DLTB features some of the best side quests in the entire franchise. The problem is that there just isn't enough of it. I want a little more of everything in this world—like making the volatile caves open and repeatable, and adding more unique random events. You can really tell that the world content suffers from the game originally being planned as a DLC. On a positive note, the actual map layout is incredible. However, the main story definitely suffers from being too short; it honestly emotionally feels like it is cut short at Act 2 instead of giving us a proper Act 3.

The game is buggy as hell.

Zombies often just stand there like scarecrows with their arms open. They get stuck mid-chase, seemingly tripping over invisible objects.

Zombies and other enemies frequently don’t animate properly while running toward me — they just kind of hover instead.

Climbing and running feel very unsmooth. There’s an unexplained lag, and I often get stuck on building corners for no reason.

Combat feels clunky.

I experienced one crash while fighting a horde.

During dialogue animations, characters sometimes stop animating completely — they just stare at me like dolls while their voices keep playing.

It’s too bad, because I played over 100 hours of Dying Light 1 and around 150 hours of Dying Light 2. I’m a big fan of the series. But with the amount of bugs, clunky combat, poor animations, and even crashes I experienced within just 120 minutes, it honestly feels unfinished.

Это возвращение к истокам, которого фанаты ждали годами. Кайл Крейн вернулся, и вместе с ним вернулась та самая густая, пугающая атмосфера, сделавшая франшизу легендарной. В 2026 году этот проект воспринимается как идеальная работа над ошибками и концентрированный опыт всего лучшего, что было в серии.

Возвращение легенды: Снова играть за Кайла Крейна - это не просто фансервис. Его новые способности, полученные после долгих лет экспериментов над ним, меняют динамику боя. Теперь ты не просто выживший, ты - настоящий хищник, способный выпускать на волю свою звериную натуру.

Кастал-Вудс: Новая локация - это глоток свежего воздуха. Вместо плотной городской застройки перед нами раскинулись мрачные леса, заброшенные промышленные зоны и таинственные исследовательские центры. Дизайн уровней мастерски сочетает классический паркур с новыми элементами окружения.

Атмосфера хоррора: Разработчики услышали фанатов и вернули в игру настоящий страх. Ночи в Кастал-Вудс по-настоящему темные и опасные. Звуки леса, тени среди деревьев и обновленные Прыгуны заставляют снова искренне бояться каждого шороха.

Транспорт: Внедрение транспортных средств здесь ощущается органично. Это не просто способ быстро попасть из точки А в точку Б, а важный элемент выживания и даже мобильная крепость, которую можно улучшать и подстраивать под свой стиль игры.

Графическое исполнение: Игра выглядит потрясающе. Густая растительность, эффекты тумана и освещение создают невероятно реалистичную и в то же время гнетущую картинку. Ощущение импакта и детализация повреждений врагов вышли на новый уровень физичности.

Сюжетная глубина: Это более личная и камерная история. Нам показывают последствия событий прошлых частей и то, как мир изменился за эти годы. Сценарий держит в напряжении, заставляя сопереживать герою, который потерял слишком много, но нашел силы бороться дальше.

Итог: Это триумфальное возвращение. Игра взяла брутальность первой части и масштаб второй, приправив это уникальными механиками «зверя». Идеальный финал (или новое начало?) истории Кайла Крейна, который заслуживает высшего балла.

[h1]消光是副好皮囊，只是皮下的那头野兽似乎真的被困住了[/h1]

作为一名预购玩家，在我游玩消光困兽的全过程中，失望几乎是贯彻始终的一大情绪——作为系列的最新作，困兽似乎一直都想要做出些改变，但其结果却无一例外地指向失败。而这种失败几乎是在游玩的第一时间就已经开始，困兽一改前作的高速跑酷，将跑酷从一种市面上独一无二的移动与攻击方式变成了某种解谜要素。

[h3]克兰老了[/h3]

作为系列的核心竞争力，在设计中，跑酷应当是一种利大于弊的设计。在消光系列这种罐头游戏中，如何减少玩家赶路的无聊时间一直是所有游戏设计者们所聚焦的地方。
消光2通过多样、高速的跑酷以及与之相称的地形设计让移动本身也成为了一种乐趣，搭配上沿途遇到的丧尸所带来的血浆刺激，让玩家一直处在兴奋中。这样的设计在困兽中被缓慢拖沓的各种基础动作所取代，高楼环伺的复杂三维空间也被压缩为了刺客信条式的街道、窗沿和屋顶三条道，更多时候甚至演都不演直接就是大平地。
2代很多时候竞速式的任务环节设计，在困兽中变成了冗长的攀爬解谜。而这些解谜只是考验玩家的眼睛，看我们能不能发现开发者涂了油漆的攀爬点；玩家的成功与失败往往不是源自个人技巧的高超与否，而是取决于油漆是否足够显眼。
在我游玩的过程中，跑图不再是享受，而是折磨。很多时候我都宁愿去开车也不愿意上房顶跑酷，以防自己又去品鉴一遍克兰那肌无力一般的攀登动作。与一代或现实中跑者的迅捷与灵巧不同，困兽中的每一次攀登都显得如此笨重且吃力。各种跑酷和攻击动作之间几乎没有打断和取消机制，以至于我总觉得困兽更像是个魂游。

[h3]坦白来说，这是我第一次觉得人类和丧尸也没什么区别[/h3]

困兽的剧情几乎没有塑造出任何一个人物，所有登场角色都好似工具人而非一个有自己性情的末日生存者，以至于时隔不到半年的我甚至记不起任何一个人名。回看一年多以前我玩的消光2，不说让人又爱又恨的哈肯“满纸荒唐言，一把辛酸泪”的立体塑造，也有拉万这样一个真挚善良的行动派。甚至于很多一笔带过的小角色也让人印象深刻，伟大的罗威中尉、可悲的阿尔贝托还有再度扛起大梁的弗兰克。尽管消光2的剧情远远说不上成功，但这些角色的身影至今仍在我的记忆中栩栩如生。在消光2中我游玩的一大动力就是剧情驱动，我渴望保护末日下一个个鲜活的人，渴望知晓那些复杂角色背后的故事，然而这种东西在困兽这一作中已经彻底消失了。而抛去人物塑造去看困兽整体的剧情，我只能说这剧情还不如不做。

[h3]“优化好”[/h3]

或许困兽确实如媒体测评视频中所讲的那样将光影与粒子特效的开销控制在了一个很不错的范围内，但那绝不意味着这是一款优化好的游戏。在我游玩时，我使用的是一台机械革命耀世16pro，搭载了4060笔电显卡和14代i9HX以及32g内存。我在整个游玩期间遭遇了极其严重的显存不足问题，百分之一low帧有时候甚至只有平均帧数的四分之一，而且不论我将画面设置调的多低都不能有效降低游戏的显存需求。作为对比，这台电脑在运行2077全高+基础光追时，启用DLSS质量和2倍帧生成仍能轻易达到70帧。消光困兽，一款在画面上并不十分出众的开放世界游戏，很多时候只能勉强够到60帧已经足以说明问题。

[b]说到底，消光困兽最大的悲剧从来不是 "做不好"，而是 "根本不想好好做"。它披着消光的精致皮囊，抽走了跑酷的灵魂，掏空了剧情的内核，最后只留下一个处处敷衍的半成品。开发者亲手把那个在哈兰市飞檐走壁、浴血搏杀的克兰，变成了连爬墙都费劲的肌无力老人；也把那个曾经独一无二的丧尸跑酷 IP，困在了罐头化量产的牢笼里。如果说前作的角色们是如同野兽般在末日里嘶吼着求生，那这一作的克兰，便是真的像只困兽一般没能改变任何东西。早在这一部发售之前，消光系列便早已身处争议，如今看来，这个IP恐怕真就要像困兽一般死在开发者的敷衍之下了。[/b]

At first I honestly wasn’t sure if Dying Light: The Beast would hit me the same way Dying Light 2 did. DL2 stayed with me emotionally because of Aiden, the choices, the endings and the feeling that my decisions actually mattered. So the beginning of The Beast felt different and took some getting used to.

But the more I played, the more I appreciated what Techland was going for.

I completed all side quests, captured all safe zones and substations, upgraded my weapons to high levels, and by the end I was completely invested. The driving, modern weapons, finishers and especially the ragdoll physics made combat feel incredibly satisfying and realistic.

What really surprised me though was the story. The game slowly builds up and then starts connecting things in ways I genuinely did not expect. Some deaths were absolutely brutal and unforgettable and the ending completely changed my opinion of the game. Seeing how it connected to Dying Light 2 got me insanely hyped.

Techland somehow keeps making endings that stay in your head long after the credits roll.

Thank you Techland for another memorable journey.

This game feels like Techland finally remembered what made [i]Dying Light[/i] so good in the first place. After [i]Dying Light 2[/i], I wasn’t sure if the series would ever really hit the same for me again, but [i]The Beast[/i] feels wayyyy closer to that original feeling I missed. The parkour feels fun again, the nights are actually intense, the combat is very brutal, the sunset is that iconic blinding gold color, and bringing Kyle Crane back in a creative way makes it feel like the franchise got some of its identity back.

It’s not 100% perfect, but with my time so far and the recent updates this is easily the most I’ve enjoyed [i]Dying Light[/i] in years. Feels like a real step back in the right direction and I can't wait to see what they do next.

Excellent game showcasing an incredible physics engine. My first Dying Light game and the one most recommended to me to play, from Stalker fans.  I played Restored Lands on Brutal and cherished the hardcore challenge.

The best melee system in any FPS I've played. Great gunplay and wonderful parkour (except the grapple hook, how do I even use this properly??). 

A ridiculously good driving/racing system. And an excellent loot system to top it off (finally we can pop the boot of a car, look for fuel in cars and see what's in the cupboard under the sink!).

You will find hiccups, but relatively few for a game this expansive and detailed. The setting is brilliant, the locations wonderfully realised, subtly guiding the player to landmarks whilst allowing heaps of room for scouting out very well-hidden and designed secrets.

Main issue I have with the game is the button mapping overload, which extends to keyboard mouse play. Having F to trigger traps can cause issues when near a trap, and trying to loot or perform a finisher, which are both also mapped to F. 

Same with the camouflage button, which in my case was also mapped to the tool button, leading to accidentally molotiving and pipebombing myself.

Trying to dodge and getting a jump input as well makes the spacebar overloaded and can result in some unwanted and potentially lethal misinputs as hops when you're trying to dodge. 

I think for non-essential inputs like triggering traps or camo, this could be bound to a different button, or else use kind of shift-button system similar to a game series like Nioh, where one button is used as a modifier for other buttons. 

In future games in this engine it'd be great to have dodge and jump on completely separate buttons. This might also be good for grapple and jump, which can also result in misinputs.

I think group finishers would be a good idea. Stamina management can be a nightmare but managing to stagger multiple enemies and put them at distance with a timely finisher would be nice. If not just getting some space back, then the ability to finish 3 or more zombies at once. 

The game seems to have a hidden combo system that triggers with certain weapons and attack sequences mixed with kicks etc (may just be damage output based). This could be more concrete, with a training dummy to practice combos on. I.e. light light kick, finisher - light charge light, finisher etc.

This all said the system as it stands is brilliant and combat basically never got tiresome, even if it was a little frustrating at times due to the dodge/jump situ and stamina management. 

Additional to this the only other issue I had was just managing equipment via the menu. The pie menu is counterintuitive at times - it'd be great if there were just more slots. And dedicated slots for various types of tools so the pie menu actually serves muscle memory. It'd be great to also be able to consume things like food from the menu without having to swap out stuff from the pie menu. Using inhalers is a great concept for a buff system but it's cumbersome and slow just swapping them out with meds/food with only 4 slots.

That's all. Incredible game. I hope it finds the success it deserves with time.

Dying Light: The Beast ist der dritte Teil der Serie und lang ersehnter direkter Nachfolger von Dying Light. Es ist die dringend benötigte Kurskorrektur nach dem eher durchwachsenen Dying Light 2, welches trotz zahlloser Updates in fast sämtlichen Belangen ein deutlicher Rückschritt zum ersten Teil war. Das Engagement der Entwickler war löblich, konnte aber grundlegende Probleme kaum beheben. DLTB zeigte schon bei seinen Trailern, dass man hier back to the roots gehen wollte. Nicht nur ist Kyle Crane zurück, auch Schusswaffen und Fahrzeuge stehen dem Spieler wieder zur Verfügung. Parkour- und Kampfsystem fühlen sich wieder richtig gut an, spielen sich snappy, präzise und dennoch wuchtig. In vielen Belangen klaut DLTB die besten Aspekte seiner Vorgänger, macht daraus jedoch mehr als die Summe seiner Teile. Das merkt man schon an der Spielwelt, die immersiv und glaubwürdig wirkt, anders als das künstlich anmutende Villedor aus DL2. Die Karte ist nicht gewaltig groß und vermeidet glücklicherweise Ladebildschirme zur Aufteilung in verschiedene Distrikte. Das kleine, urige Land Castor Woods bietet dabei angemessen abwechslungsreiche Areale, wirkt aber keinesfalls wie ein aufgesetzter Theme Park, der nur Settings abhaken will. Egal ob Altstadt, Wald, Gebirge oder Ackerland, alles ist wunderschön und authentisch in Szene gesetzt und ein gelungenes Beispiel für eine mittelgroße, aber hochdetaillierte Open World. Bezaubernde Vistas und Landschaften wecken dabei schon oft aus großer Entfernung das Interesse des Spielers, was die Erkundung der Spielwelt ungezwungen und organisch macht. Das Gesamtbild wird durch die stimmungsvolle Beleuchtung und eindrucksvollen Wettereffekte zusätzlich abgerundet. Lange hat mich kein Spiel mehr so stark mit seinen Regenschauern und Gewittern beeindruckt. Zu Fuß kommt man dabei in Castor Woods ebenso gut wie mit PKWs voran, welche aber anders als in Dying Light: The Following randomisierte, respawnende Verbrauchsobjekte sind. Sämtliche Mechaniken rund um den persönlichen Buggy von Crane fehlen leider, was ein unerwarteter Rückschritt im Spieldesign ist.
Egal wie aber erkundet wird, die phänomenale Musik macht es stets zum großen Vergnügen. Orchestrale wie elektronische Stücke sind fantastisch, erzeugen jederzeit stets die richtige Stimmung. Atmosphärische Tracks machen das Erkunden der Wildnis zu einem geradezu meditativen Erlebnis, anmutige und sentimentale Klänge beklagen die verlorene alte Welt, gruselige Stücke erzeugen Gänsehaut für die finstersten Momente. Und auch die fetzigen Beats bei Kämpfen sind zurückgekehrt. Das generelle Sounddesign kann sich problemlos mit der hervorragenden Musik messen und erzeugt mühelos eine immersive, dichte Stimmung. Schrittgeräusche, die Interaktion mit Gegenständen, hektische Gefechte, das Stöhnen der Zombies in den Straßen, raschelnde Blätter, peitschender Höhenwird, entfernte Klänge des Gebirges oder Schusswechsel in weiter Ferne, nichts wirkt deplatziert. Auch die Kämpfe wertet das Sounddesign enorm auf, lässt zersplitternde und brechende Knochen, reißendes Fleisch und blubbernde Eingeweide ebenso unappetitlich wie beeindruckend erklingen. Die Atmosphäre der Open World wird so sehr durch Musik, Sounddesign und Environmental Storytelling getragen, wie tausend Seiten Dialog es nicht könnten. Castor Woods wirkt trotz seiner natürlichen Idylle dabei oft sehr beklemmend. Ein Ort, über dem stets die bedrohliche Stimmung eines unmittelbaren Unheils liegt. Überwältigender Horror, der hinter jeder Ecke lauern könnte, ganz sicher jedoch nachts sein Antlitz zeigt. Der Einbruch der Nacht ist wieder absolut genial inszeniert. Abends flaut zunächst der Wind ab, dann piept der Alarm der Armbanduhr, eine beklemmende Stille mit ominösem Rumpeln in den Bergen tritt ein, bevor die markerschütternden Schreie der Schattenjäger ihr Erscheinen ankündigen. Dieser ganze Ablauf ist ein Beispiel von perfekt geplantem und exakt bemessenem Horror. Er funktioniert perfekt und steht im reizvollen Kontrast zu den beruhigen Klängen der Natur am Tag.
Die Nacht lockt bei großem Risiko wieder mit großen Belohnungen. Die nächtlich verdoppelten XP und seltene Ressourcen beschleunigen das Vorankommen bei dringend benötigten Upgrades. Auf den höchsten Schwierigkeitsgraden wird DLTB zwar lange kein Soulslike, machte mir aber schnell deutlich, dass man keinen Vorteil ausschlagen und im Zweifel lieber gut equipped und überlevelt sein will. In kleinerem Format bieten die zurückkehrenden Dark Zones die gleiche Erfahrung, ködern zudem mit einzigartigen und Belohnungen. Leider werden die Dark Zones schnell repetitiv und öde. Ein Dilemma, da man auf die wertvollen Ressourcen angewiesen ist, dafür jedoch Langeweile ertragen muss. 
Die primäre Gameplay-Formel wird dadurch aber kaum runtergezogen, welche durch das gelungene Kampfsystem glücklicherweise stark aufgewertet wird. Kämpfe sind hart, oft ressourcenintensiv, dabei aber stets fair und nachvollziehbar. Wenn man stirbt, geschieht dies meist blitzschnell. In den frühen Phasen der Story ist man noch schwach und sehr auf fleißiges Plündern, vorsichtiges Vorgehen und die geschickte Nutzung der Umgebung angewiesen, bevor sich ein angenehmer Power Creep einschleicht und man vom Gejagten zum Jäger wird. Selbst in Bosskämpfen bekommen wir dabei praktisch komplett freie Hand, dürfen Nahkampfwaffen in jeder Situation Seite an Seite mit Schusswaffen, Sprengstoffen und anderen exotischen Werkzeugen nutzen. Das Gunplay ist solide, aber das Hauptfeature bleibt natürlich das elaborierte Nahkampfsystem. Das rudimentäre aber überraschend funktionale Schleichsystem hat mich beeindruckt und wer gerne mit Bögen kämpft, wird hier voll auf seine Kosten kommen. Bei den Skills gibt es alte Bekannte und so manche spaßige Neuerung. Die große Attraktion ist natürlich der titelgebende Biest-Modus, welcher als temporärer Power-Boost funktioniert, eigene Skills mit sich bringt, dabei aber leider etwas hinter meinen Erwartungen zurückbleibt und schnell zur routinemäßigen Mechanik ohne echte Nachteile wird. Ich hätte mir eine tiefergehende Einbindung durch die Story gewünscht.
Denn die Story ist auch in diesem Teil der Reihe die objektiv größte Schwäche, zum Glück aber weit von einem Totalausfall entfernt. Die Geschichte bleibt angemessen spannend und man will immer erfahren, was als nächstes geschieht. Charaktere und Plot funktionieren, bleiben dabei nachvollziehbar und interessant, anders als im oft sehr linkisch geschriebenen DL2. Weniger ist manchmal mehr und so bekommen wir keine großen Fraktionsmechaniken und Entscheidungen geboten, sondern eine sehr bodenständige und persönliche Geschichte, die extrem von Kyle als bekanntem Protagonisten profitiert und bewusst einen kleineren Fokus setzt. Kyle funktioniert als Charakter auf einer fundamentalen, menschlichen Ebene und wächst dem Spieler richtig ans Herz. Seine Vergangenheit plagt ihn, aber auch die Gegenwart vermag ihn zu quälen. Ein paar Twists waren vorhersehbar, andere weniger. Manche Handlungsstränge verlaufen etwas ziellos und inkonsequent und einige Charaktere hätte ich mir pointierter gewünscht. Man bekommt das Gefühl, dass nicht alles auserzählt wurde und der Plot manche Figuren noch etwas besser hätte ausarbeiten können. Es kommt hinzu, dass die Handlung sich gegen Ende regelrecht überschlägt, obwohl es vorher eher gemächlich zuging. Das ist aber nur holpriges Pacing und grundlegend ist die Story gelungen, immer wieder unerwartet reif und berührend.

Insgesamt bin ich sehr zufrieden mit Dying Light: The Beast. Ich bin froh, dass es nicht wie ursprünglich geplant als Addon für das eher missglückte Dying Light 2 endete, sondern zum eigenständigen Spiel aufgewertet wurde. Es ist exakt, was die Reihe zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt gebraucht hat. Nicht alles ist perfekt, doch zusammengenommen macht Dying Light: The Beast so unerwartet viel Spaß, dass es für mich zum absoluten Überraschungshit geworden ist.

Игра имеет спорные моменты, которые заставляют сомневаться в том, что это полноценная игра, а не дополнение (DLC). Сюжет чрезмерно растянут, и основное внимание уделено беготне по локациям.

Положительным моментом является возвращение к стилю боёвки и физики из первой части. Однако в игре изначально мало контента, а дополнения в патчах кажутся незначительными. В сравнении с первой частью, где дополнительного контента было больше, чем основного сюжета, здесь ситуация обратная.

После нескольких прохождений на высоком уровне сложности можно с уверенностью сказать, что назвать это полноценной игрой сложно. Разработчикам стоило бы выпустить это как DLC, а не как новую часть по полной стоимости.

Тем не менее, если брать игру по скидке, она может оказаться неплохой, особенно для совместного прохождения. В плане геймплея, механик и графики вопросов нет — всё отлично. За более чем 100 часов игры баги не встречались (на релизе, возможно, они были, но были исправлены патчами).

Надеюсь, разработчики добавят действительно стоящий контент, а не только косметические изменения. После двух прохождений для получения достижений в игре может стать скучновато из-за отсутствия новых занятий.

Считаю, что игра приносит удовольствие, но не стоит полной стоимости. Тем не менее, игру рекомендую для проведения времени в компании пары друзей!

If you're a fan of the previous games and have an itch for more Dying Light, then maybe give this one a try if it's on sale. Otherwise, I can't recommend this game. 

A lot of my frustrations stem from a lack of visual cues that could give the player a better idea of what the game designer wants them to do. For example, part of this game is climbing buildings, but not everything is climbable. This is fine but there needs to be a clear distinction between what objects on a building can and can't be climbed. When everything is the same poop color theme, the player has to spend extra time trying to figure out what to do. 

I might forgive the lack of visual cues and attribute my negative experience unique to me but the other part of my frustrations with this game is poor mission design. The prime example of this is one mission where the objective is time sensitive. You're required drive to location and have to exit the the vehicle in a specific area otherwise the game will tell you need to get back into the vehicle - even if you're already clearly at the objective. The objective is within a house and your only indicator is that you're within the objective area and that you have to look for the room you need to go to while the timer is running out. I failed this multiple times because the house is empty and the there's no clear indication of what room I need to go into. I ultimately had to look up a youtube guide to learn that I'm supposed to open door immediately on my left after entering the house to trigger completion of the objective. Looking at the comments of the video, my experience was definitely not unique. This mission could benefit from a visual cue of what door the player needs to open or simply trigger the objective complete once entering the house and trigger the cut scene.

Как человек, которого Dying Light затянула ещё с первой части и не отпускает до сих пор, я просто обязан высказаться. The Beast — это именно то, чего душа просила. Я не спал до трёх ночи, проходил миссию за миссией, и оторваться было нереально.

Смотрите, по сюжету: Крейн возвращается, и он теперь не просто выживший с битой, он сам стал чем-то бóльшим. В нём просыпается звериная сущность, и это не просто галочка для сюжета — это реально работает. Ты носишься по карте, разрываешь заражённых голыми руками, рычишь, прыгаешь как одержимый, и оно ощущается чертовски круто. Как будто тебе наконец дали ту самую силу, которой так не хватало, когда ты прятался по крышам в первой части.

Мир, кстати, не пытается притворяться огромным ради галочки. Он камерный, плотный, каждый уголок чем-то занят. Исследуешь — и постоянно натыкаешься на какие-то детали, заметки, истории. Если не хочется идти по сюжету, можно просто гулять ночью и проверять нервы на прочность. Ночь тут всё так же прекрасна в своей жестокости. Звук поставлен так, что ты сидишь в наушниках и реально вертишь головой на каждый шорох.

Отдельно скажу про атмосферу. Она гнетущая, мрачная, но при этом красивая до мурашек. Закаты над мёртвым городом, туман в лесу, полуразрушенные дома — рука так и тянется делать скриншоты. Я не фанат фоторежимов обычно, но тут реально залипал.

Косяки есть, куда без них. Текстуры иногда подводят, пару раз было забавное, когда враг застрял в стене и дёргался как в конвульсиях. Но после первого патча стало уже лучше, и это вообще не мешает удовольствию. Ночные миссии всё так же выжигают нервы — если не любите хорроры, может быть тяжеловато. Но это же Dying Light, тут по-другому и быть не должно.

В итоге: это не просто игра на вечер, это полноценное возвращение туда, где хорошо и страшно одновременно. Если скучали по Крейну, по ночным забегам, по этой уникальной смеси паркура и зомби-апокалипсиса — берите не думая. Я уже часа тридцать наиграл и останавливаться не собираюсь.

Solid experience so far, its very much what you would expect from a Dying Light experience.
While its way better than the second game in almost all regards; it can't beat the iconic nature of the first game. 
The Story is fine? It's better than 2 and more memorable but thats not saying much. 
It's pretty campy and there are some wonderfully cheesy lines from Crane when he goes Beast mode in story moments, but thats kinda a part of the fun, nobody really expects a masterpiece in storytelling.
It has it's moments but mostly its what you're gonna expect from DL (Action movie get the big bad and save the day while fighting your own demons type story)
It held my attention for the most part, but I was more curious and having fun than actually emotionally invested.

A few things that are massively improved from the second game would be:
1. Actual pitch-black dark and terrifying night gameplay that skips the UV mechanics of the second game that eventually bec ome redundant mid-to-late game.
2. Way better gunplay in every way (could use some more variety however)
3. Better feeling melee combat with improved ragdoll physics that they somehow managed to mess up a little in DL2.
4. Bigger focus on zombies and not humans like the second game while not cutting out what made human encounters good.
5. Really good weather effects: the rain was absolutley gorgeus, the day/night cycle felt fleshed out and it was very clear even without looking at your watch when the night was coming.
6. More grounded map without massive immersion-breaking glowing chemical spills. The map is truly beautiful and packed with cool locations.

I would've liked a bigger map or maybe even a second one in theme with how the first and second game setup their maps. While there is A LOT of content here I can still sense the DNA of the DLC it was supposed to be at first.
In hindsight I probably should've paced myself a little, I ended up finding all of the safe spots before I was even done with the main plot and retracing the map for story quests felt a bit like a grind by the end.

Either way I had a great time and I loved being Crane again and slapping the undead around like they owed him money.

In this game, the characters are all painfully shallow, with no real friends or relationships developing at all. Kyle is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to everyone, and they treat him much the same way. [h2]Барон бежал в страхе, когда увидел, какой урон лезет из Крейна.[/h2]

Ну что ж, времени в игре проведено достаточно, большая часть контента пощупана — можно и пару слов-то написать.

Между тем: это первая игра, которую брал на релизе. После ниочёмошной второй части на Биста особых надежд не возлагал. Но, видимо, зря. Получилось крайне годно.

Боевка ощущается как реальная боевка, а не как бессвязное рубилово. Более детализировали повреждения по зомбарям, вес оружия теперь ощущается куда лучше. Разнообразие расчленёнки и добивок невелико, но и не одно на всю игру. К количеству оружия вопросов нет: милишка всё также доминирует, но и с огнестрелом не обделили — первую пушку получить можно уже на первых часах игры. Форма зверя — кайф в чистом виде: в боях эффективно, визуально — шик.

Сюжетка напоминает по повествованию первую часть. Коротенькая, линейная, пусть и до жути банальная, но цепляет. Сайды также очень добротные. Их немного, проходятся быстро, истории интересные, поэтому пропускать не стоит. Музыка тематически вписалась везде просто великолепно, да и сами треки балдёжные.

[h3]Теперь по минусам:[/h3]

Самый главный, как по мне, недостаток — количество контента. Уже после релиза игру активно допиливали: коллабы, уровни легенды, НГ+, новые уровни сложности, всяческие ивенты. Но вся их суть завязана на гринде. Основная сюжетка проходится в спокойном темпе часов за 8. Столько же или чуть больше — на сайды. Дальше — гринд. Гринд легендарного оружия, гринд платины, гринд уровней легенды, гринд тех ивентов, на которых уже почти никто не принимал участия, перепрохождения на НГ+ на других сложностях. С недавней обновы и вовсе — перепройти игру в ещё более хард-режиме, а для платины… снова закрывать сохранку на 100% и гриндить.

В общем, к чему это — растягивать пребывание в игре за счёт добавления только лишь фарма — идея не очень, мягко говоря. Да и если брать в учёт, что она изначально планировалась как DLC, то ситуация ещё хуже.

Если жаждете выбить платину — придётся жёстко фармить. Игра слишком привязана к этому: придётся буквально гоняться за каждой коллекционкой в разные уголки карты.

[h3]По итогу:[/h3]

За свои 100+ часов успел пройти сюжетку 6 раз, поднять 300 легенды, разжиться достаточным количеством лута и, самое главное, получить удовольствие от игры (даже при наличии узкого разнообразия контента).

Если вам в принципе нравится DL — можете брать, пройти сюжетку и погонять в коопе будет самое то. Новшествами по сравнению с двумя другими частями Зверь не блещет, так что, если были мысли на счёт этого — можно забыть. Придётся она по душе или нет — вопрос к вашему отношению к серии и желанию найти тут что-то своё.

What a BEAST of a game. The developers absolutely nailed what they were going for with this. Brutal, kinetic, propulsive, and get this—pure fun. Eurojank, but without the jank!

If anything, I think Dying Light: The Beast is underrated. If Capcom or id Software released this it would be held up as a blockbuster. 

It reminds me a lot of a more violent (and frankly just better) version of what Far Cry could have become. 

The climbing and movement mechanics are the star of the show, and it just feels so good to be storming around the environment. That alongside the gore tech for lopping off zombie limbs. 

The graphics are quality too—this is exactly the kind of game some devs would have tried to use UE5 for, and it would have been a mess. Instead we get a custom engine designed to do what it does well. The European forest and mountain vibe, plus the concentrated old city and industrial areas, all feel like someone actually cared.

Even the story isn’t too bad. I mean, it’s not what I came for. But again, I quite liked a few of the twists and turns. -Достаточно короткий сюжет, но с учетом того, что игра планировалась как DLC данная проблема не столь велика.

- И также хочу выделить то, что в игре встречаются баги, но думаю разработчики это исправят.
Теперь перейдем к плюсам данного проекта:
- Невероятную атмосферу пост-апокалипсиса и ужаса: постоянно встречающиеся зомби, брошенные дома, а также фирменную часть всех игр Dying Light - Ночь, ночью игра становится совсем другой, вместо грозного хищника, мы играем за жертву, постоянный страх нарваться на прыгунов, погони и чувства, что ты никто против них - дает о себе знать.

- Систему паркура - это одно из самых главных достоинств игр Dying Light, паркур в этой части менее динамичный чем в прошлых частях, но все равно сделан и выглядит потрясно.
- Красивый и разнообразный открытый мир локации старого города, фермы, парки выглядят современно и графически приятно, нельзя упустить наличие в мире различных побочных активностей и случайных встреч.
Теперь хочу сделать общий вывод и рассказать в каких случаях стоит покупать игру, а в каких стоит подумать
  Игру стоит покупать если :
- Вы любите экшен, эта игра- отличное решение для покупки если вам нравятся игры в этом жанре.
- Нравится атмосфера пост-апокалипсиса - вам однозначно зайдет.
- Любите ощущение ужаса, неизбежности - эта игра однозначно напомнит вам о том, что такое страх.
Стоит задуматься о покупке если :
- Вам не нравится постоянный экшен : кровь, жестокие добивания, интенсивные бои - эта игра явно не для вас.
- Вы являетесь слишком впечатлительным - в игре встречается множество жестоких сцен, вам врятли это доставит удовольствие.
- Вы боитесь высоты,  - в игре есть паркур и это одна из главных механик игры, и если вы категорически не приемлете падений, прыжков с высоток - эта игра вам не зайдет

The overall presentation of Castor woods is genuinely beautiful. It made me stop and just sit on a roof or hill side and watch the sun rise and sunset. Even the when it rains its just so atmospheric. The contrast of daytime and nighttime is honestly master craft from this dev team. It might be in my head, but this is how it feels to me. The daytime is bright and easy going, mornings are so pretty and calm but there's always the threat of zombies. You fall into a routine of scavenging and killing zombies and doing jobs. Then The sun starts to set. Everything gets this golden orange glow, the tree leaves radiate the suns light, the clouds have almost this painterly look. Then the light starts to fade. The music gets more early and your watch beeps a warning. As the light fades, what was 10 seconds ago so pretty now starts to get scary. Without the suns warm light, the mountains almost feel like your trapped in this valley, the sun retreating from this place. The trees have no shape and are these rustling blobs of darkness that could hide anything. Zombie groans can be heard all around but they blend into the tall grass and bushes. The music becomes hostile and the atmosphere is oppressive. The first nightfall I had, I rushed to a safe spot hunter stand and legit scrambled up it sweating running from volatiles. The only things I could see was what my flashlight cone could light up. After activating the safe zone I just stood there overlooking the valley that was once so pretty I stopped to take pictures now had me frozen in fear of the unknown. 


The nighttime has made me feel scared like Dying light 1 first did. Also Because crane is not Aiden Bo Baden with a glider and an entire downtown to run away in, You will be gangstalked by the volatiles. Let me be real with you. That first shotgun you get will not help you. I wish I had clip of the first time I tube dumped the shotgun into a volatile only for it to be even more pissed and its 3 friends that heard what I did came in and ripped me in half.

Honestly, smaller scope makes this game a "finishable product". The beast has just enough content, for me at least, that I got a solid 38 hours. I skipped a couple quests that rewarded just xp and did not look for any of the scavenger hunt scribble drawing pages that you can pick up. So if you do everything you could easily get 40 to 45 hours of content. I actually wanted to see how side quests resolved and was interested the entire time, I know shocker for a story game. I cant say the same for a single part of DL2. I legit cannot remember a single thing about DL2's story or sidequests. I still can remember a lot of DL1 even after 10 years. The Beast maybe wont stick with you for that long, but it is miles better than dl2 on every front other than parkour. 

The parkour is not a focus at all in combat or traversal for a good 60 percent of the map. They give you a grappling hook and I felt like spider man in a corn field, like oh wow I can swing from a single tree before face planting. It's really sad when a great series gets turned into a steaming pile of what it once was. Dying Light was a great game. Dying Light 2 was perfection itself. The Beast, does away with everything I loved about the first two. 

Did you enjoy the flowing parkour over rooftops? Gone. The only rooftops are on a hillside city that takes up maybe 10% of the map and since all the buildings are on different levels there is no more jumping between them without either climbing or falling to your death. The rest of the map is flat or forest which requires no parkour. 

Did you enjoy a well rounded leveling skill system? Say goodbye to that. The skills in this game mostly seem useless, nothing you grow into is exciting or enhances your experience beyond basic powering up of what you already have. 

Did you enjoy the thrill of going out at night and trying to avoid volatiles and then the tense chases when they saw you? This game makes going out at night a death sentence. Volatiles just spawn close to you everywhere you go. Their wandering patterns never take them far enough away from you or each other to actually get by them. Oh, and the "Master Stealth" skill? Does absolutely nothing. Every enemy can see you perfectly in pitch blackness. 

The grapple hook? utterly pointless in a massive mostly flat partially forested map.

The interesting power puzzles? Gone. Now you just have to clear out the fenced area around the substations and flip a switch. 

About the only thing they added to this game that is remotely fun is driving trucks through large groups of zombies but even that gets old after a while. 

I don't know who was responsible for this utter disappointment but they ruined a beautiful franchise.

Was sceptical at first, but bought the game after they announced the Restored Land game mode, and that the game was on discount.

The good:

Everything good about DL1, smooth parkour, nights are terrifying, zombie-killing is very gory and satisfying. With all the new Chimeras, and zombie types, somehow Volatiles still remain as the scariest part of the game.

Puzzles: A lot more puzzles compared to DL1 during quests, or clearing stations, unlocking safe zones, which often involves parkour, sneaking, or looking through documents etc, initially quite annoying as there is zero hand-holding, they gave you the task, and you're just expected to solve it, no markers, no tips. The first few puzzles encountered I was so confused and had to look up youtube guides to solve, but after a while I got used to how they design these puzzles then it became much more easier to solve, and yet still satisfying after solving each one. The parkouring puzzles are especially fun and most are unique from one another.

Story is simple, serviceable. Its interesting enough to not make you skip it. Characters are also simple by design, no complex character arcs, predictable betrayals. Always seems black and white, not much gray areas when it comes to the story and characters, which wasnt a bad thing, considering that's not the main point of the game that focuses on killing zombies and parkour.

The beast mode feels amazing, clawing through hordes of zombies, hulk jumping around the field, slamming the ground with shockwaves, along with cinematic finishers, such as pulling of zombie heads, punching through the chest, smashing a volatile head repeatedly on the ground, always satisfying. Easily one of the best feature in the game.

Restored land game mode: Zombies actually stayed dead and clearing zones feels amazing, felt like actual progression when playing instead of "killing them because they're in my way" or "vaulting over zombies cuz they just come back anyways". Certain resources are limited (such as batteries) so that you actually need to be careful not to waste your resources unnecessarily (though there's so much food lying around it technically negates the whole hunger bar addition).

The bad (or not so good):

Chimeras: The new addition to the game which are basically "boss battles" but most of it is just a copy paste of existing zombie types and amp up the damage and health. On top of that, they all have the "summon adds" mechanic which is just annoying and doesnt add any depth to the fight, just adds clutter and annoyance espcially when you're focusing on the boss and a random biter grabs you and the boss lands a lethal 70% damage hit on you. Half of the chimeras are just big zombies that charge at you and smashes ground, and the other half are slightly more memorable such as Wraith with invisibility, Matriarch with Mist and the Toxin.

Human enemies: Just annoying to deal with in general, melee fighters can dodge everything and parry everything almost 80% of the time, while range enemies often you cant even see them and just get shot from no where.

Skill tree is overly simplified with 0 customization, its basically level up get this skill, might as well just remove the entire interface and just give different skills each time we level. Despite my praise for the beast mode, there's so much more they couldve added to the skill tree but didnt such as additional skills like thunderclap, forward pounces etc.

0 customizations for guns/ranged weapons. No silencers, extended mags etc. Guns are pretty boring in general, bows are good for sniping silently only. Very underwhelming overall but then again, most players will rely on melee weapons anyways so not the biggest deal, would've been cool though to have mods for guns.

Volatiles nest still makes no sense/doesnt work/bugged? I have not encountered a single nest that's active at night aside from the main story. Good thing is it doesnt really impact much on my enjoyment of the game, just feels rather pointless.

Lack of side quests around the old town (the main city), aside from being the heart of the main story, along with the best designed location compared to the outskirts of the town, it has very little side quests (about 3 if I remembered correctly) and they all start from the town hall (which is the main building). There were no quests from random survivors outside of the hall, or just random encounters, (like going into a random building and finding a kid in the closet hiding from dad-turned zombie), which makes the town feels more empty/hollow despite having more zombies around. However, there's decent amount of side quests after reaching the exiled cave which is the second main base for the main story.

Overall still a really good game, but still cant say I enjoyed this more than DL1 which till date is still a masterpiece, also considering DL1 costs only a fraction of this game. The game has at least 30-40 worth of meaningful content (main quests, side quests, clearing safe zones and dark zones) and can easily reach 70-80 hours if you plan to 100% the game, those who said there's too little content and stops after 15 hours basically just rushed the main story to the end without doing much of anything else. The game however, still costs $60 which is on the pricier side, and if you're comparing to other games in the same price range (such as Cyberpunk 2077), its hard to justify paying full price for the game. I would say, its definitely worth getting at a discounted price, or if you're dying for a dying light game that feels like the first, then get it, you wont regret it.

I wish there was a 'Mixed' option for Steam reviews, as this game falls into that category for me. I *LOVE* DL1 & 2.

Overall, the game felt more like an addon/DLC akin to DL1's The Following.

The story and voice acting were (again) very good. This was the game's strong suit.

Gameplay-wise ... I just didn't 'feel' it. 

The parkour felt a bit clunky, I didn't ever feel like I 'flowed'. I didn't enjoy the map anywhere near as much as DL2's with its massive verticality, and I wonder if the design of the map made parkour feel quite stop/start. Also, I was *never* sure if I would make a jump/grab ... auto-grab was very hit and miss, and some ledges seemed easily reachable, but apparently there was no *insert code that makes a ledge grabbable*. The *only* parkour improvement over DL2 is the lack of the stamina bar for climbing.

The only use I found for the grapple was yanking Zs and headstomping them. That *was* fun (at first) ...

I found the combat quite flat, with the environmental effects on weapons and in the world being very underwhelming. No 'dropkick' manoeuvre, only a vault/dropkick. As you level up you need 2 headstomps to kill a downed enemy ... headstomp should *ALWAYS* be a finisher! I played Dead Island 2 last year, and the combat in that game (including environmental fx) really flowed and was real fun.

The Beast mode ... again, I found it really underwhelming. It took a lot to charge up, then was expended too quickly, even after I had fully upgraded The Beast skill branch. Maybe the Legend levels where they allow you to speed up charging and prolong The Beast mode make you feel like The Beast ... but you'd need at least another playthrough to get the XP to bump those skills up.

I really disliked the driving, and the trucks don't handle well enough (they turn like an oil tanker!) for the racing quest to feel fun - I completely swerved them (pun intended!).

Although I thought the map wasn't particularly large, it felt quite empty. I will say that the different zones (town/forest/farm/industrial) did all have distinct designs.

The crafting/upgrading weapons and items was a big downgrade from DL2 (I *LOVE* looting and hoarding components!).

I played @2560x1080 with settings maxed and upscaling 'Quality' and consistently hit 60fps.

Overall I expected more from the gameplay and was quite disappointed, but I'm glad I played the game for the story and world building which it does *really* well.

Despite my 'mixed' review, I look forward to the next installment in the DL universe.

Após ter jogado mais de 100hrs e ter feito 100% das conquistas, acho que posso dar a minha opinião sincera do jogo.


O Dying Light The Best, não é ruim, mas está longe de chegar aos pés do primeiro.

Primeiro ponto: dá pra ver claramente que esse dying light era pra ser uma DLC, pois o jogo é pequeno demais, se você for tentar terminar o jogo sem fazer 100% das conquistas, você acaba em 16hrs ou até menos que isso, você percebe que foi um conteúdo mastigado e que o protagonista não era pra ser o Crane, eles só reimplementaram o Crane novamente pra vender o jogo, pois sabiam que o Crane seria um chamariz pra vendas, coisa que deu muito certo.

Segundo pronto: ao contrário do primeiro, nesse Dying Light falta aquele cenário caótico do primeiro jogo, aquele cenário de destruição, aquele bloom alaranjado que dava um toque de um mundo pós apocalíptico.

Terceiro ponto: você usa pouco parkour, pra ser mais específico, você usa o parkour somente dentro da cidade, a cidade é minúscula, 10% de cidade e o restante do mapa é só mato, e isso acaba tirando toda a proposta do primeiro jogo, e acaba que se torna cansativo demais ter que ficar andando de um lado pra outro num mapa totalmente vazio sem nada pra fazer.

Quarto ponto: eles colocaram missões muito distantes pra prolongar o tempo de jogo, mas acaba que isso é totalmente desnecessário e cansativo, você corre km, pra pegar um item pro cara que está na cidade, leva esse item pro cara, depois ele pede pra você voltar no mesmo local pra pegar mais um item, e cara, isso se torna enjoativo demais, chegou uma hora que eu não via o momento de acabar esse jogo e desinstalar da minha máquina.

Quinto ponto: a história do jogo é rushada o tempo todo, e diferente do primeiro jogo, você não consegue se apegar a nenhum personagem aqui, nem mesmo ao próprio Crane, são personagens sem sal, que não tem desenvolvimento algum durante todo jogo.

Sexto ponto: o Crane continua o mesmo bobalhão do primeiro jogo, acreditando nos outros e se ferrando depois, só que aqui é ainda pior. Fulano te trai, você fica put0 com o fulano e no final do nada esse fulano aparece te pedindo desculpas e o Crane simplesmente vai lá e aceita as desculpas como se nada tivesse acontecido, e isso acontece com mais de um personagem, e você fica tipo, "Tá, esse fulano me traiu e só vou aceitar sem mais nem menos".

Sétimo ponto: o principal vilão do jogo que é o barão, ele só aparece duas vezes no jogo, no início e no final, fora isso, você só fica ouvindo os outros personagens falar dele, o barão fez isso, o barão fez aquilo, o barão está fazendo uma nova pesquisa, e em nenhum momento você tromba com ele novamente sem ser nesses dois momentos, muito diferente do primeiro Dying Light, que o Rais o tempo todo é presente, fica te provocando, mata seus colegas na sua frente, faz o inferno na sua vida só pra ver você ficar put0 com ele, mas nesse aqui não existe isso, e acaba que você não cria aquela raiva do vilão, pois ele não é presente igual ao Rais. 

Oitavo ponto: o final desse jogo é que nem novela mexicana, um vilão que se acha o rei da cocada preta, que se gaba do poder que tem, e só nesse momento ele tenta fazer uma única m3rd4 pra tentar fazer você ficar com raiva dele, e cara, ficou um final bem b0st4, sem contar também uma personagem que a gente ajuda ela, pra ela conseguir um poder f0d1d0, que de acordo com ela aquele poder iria mudar tudo no jogo, pra chegar no final ela não fazer nada com o poder.


Então, o jogo tenta ser o que foi o primeiro mas não consegue. São cenários vazios, personagens sem desenvolvimento algum, vilão sem presença alguma, final bem m3rd4 e pouco tempo de jogo pelo preço que pedem nele.

Não vou indicar o jogo da forma que se encontra devido todas essas falhas, recomendo esperar uma baita promoção, e se tivesse uma recomendação razoável, essa seria minha recomendação pra esse jogo.

What really stands out is the tension and atmosphere. Exploring abandoned areas, scavenging for supplies, and trying to survive against stronger infected creates a great mix of excitement and fear.

Overall, Dying Light: The Beast is a fantastic experience for both long-time fans and newcomers. It keeps what made the original games great while adding enough new features to make it feel fresh.

作为原本定位为《消逝的光芒2》DLC的《消逝的光芒：困兽》（下称《困兽》），据说是因为体量越做越大，才最终转正成为了一部外传性质的正式作品。 拥有《消逝的光芒2：终极版》的玩家可以免费获得该游戏，但该版本目前已经在Steam停售。 虽然一开始《困兽》是作为《消逝的光芒2》的DLC而立项的，《困兽》的剧情时间线也处于《消逝的光芒2》之后，但本作玩家将要扮演的主角却回归了一代的“哈兰战神”——凯尔·克兰。
在一代结局中变身为夜魔之后，克兰被“男爵”所领导的势力捕获，送至了欧洲阿尔卑斯山下一个名为河狸谷的小镇，并遭受了十多年人体实验的折磨，成为了体内同时具有人类和夜魔两种DNA的“混种”，但至少恢复了人类的理智和形态。
现在，克兰逃出来了，猜猜他要找谁去寻仇?
在复仇之前，让我们先来深入认识一下克兰目前所在的河狸谷。
就像开头所说的那样，这是一个坐落在阿尔卑斯山下的小镇，主要发展以自然风光为主题的旅游业，河狸波波就是它们的吉祥物，因此城镇规模不大，大部分地区建筑密度也不甚高，更不像二代一样的到处都是高楼大厦，不过不少建筑都依然能够进入探索，也有沼泽、农田、森林等较为多样的地形地貌。
在复仇之前，让我们先来深入认识一下克兰目前所在的河狸谷。
就像开头所说的那样，这是一个坐落在阿尔卑斯山下的小镇，主要发展以自然风光为主题的旅游业，河狸波波就是它们的吉祥物，因此城镇规模不大，大部分地区建筑密度也不甚高，更不像二代一样的到处都是高楼大厦，不过不少建筑都依然能够进入探索，也有沼泽、农田、森林等较为多样的地形地貌。在复仇之前，让我们先来深入认识一下克兰目前所在的河狸谷。
就像开头所说的那样，这是一个坐落在阿尔卑斯山下的小镇，主要发展以自然风光为主题的旅游业，河狸波波就是它们的吉祥物，因此城镇规模不大，大部分地区建筑密度也不甚高，更不像二代一样的到处都是高楼大厦，不过不少建筑都依然能够进入探索，也有沼泽、农田、森林等较为多样的地形地貌。另外，我强烈推荐大家去好好体验河狸谷中的支线任务，因为本作的支线任务不仅没有大量重复的通马桶内容，在剧情方面还能够提供十分充足的情绪价值。
比如在接取任务时要是碰上一些强人所难的要求，克兰会化身玩家的嘴替，主动直接地开口质疑任务的必要性，以欲拒还迎的手段让对面放低身段，以恳求的姿态请求自己的帮助。在任务提供了一些分支选项，并且玩家进行了选择以后，也少有人会以道德标兵的姿态跳出来指责玩家，而是会代入克兰的视角为玩家辩解。而完成任务以后，任务发布者还会不吝自己的夸赞之语，来感激玩家所付出的苦功。这些方面的改变，让《困兽》里玩家完成支线任务所能带来的正反馈直接拉满，甚至能让相对平淡的跑图环节变成调剂剧情节奏的手段，反倒是让人有些意犹未尽，只愈发觉得支线任务数量太少了。
再者说了，本作的载具刷新点几乎算得上是随处可见，点出技能后载具自带的油量差不多足够玩家开遍全图，上车后还有全息导航实时指引任务路线。虽说这样设计确实削减了不少跑酷玩法的戏份，但奈何河狸谷本来就有一半的地方没有任何建筑，就算是成龙恐怕也很难只靠双脚，就能在除了树木就是丧尸的地方跑酷吧。除非他也拥有本作的辅助跑酷道具——“爪钩”。
本作爪钩的运作机制和二代一样，需要通过消耗体力来发动。其拉力虽然不足以让角色直接位移到目标地点，但能通过摆荡来提升速度和缩进距离，也可以通过朝高处连续出钩的方式来快速上楼。只不过由于体力消耗被提高（也可能是体力上限下降）了，主角能够连续出钩的次数也大幅减少了。除此以外，爪钩还能直接将敌人钩倒在地，点出倒地处决技能后能够快速清理杂兵。
另外，滑翔伞并不会在本作出场。　而在基础系统层面，制作组的选择是让《困兽》回归初代那种偏向生存体验的底层设计。
不仅制造各种武器道具的材料需求所有增加，近战武器的耐久也会随着使用不断减少，玩家从一个拿枪的敌人身上搜到的弹药同样变得非常吝啬，通常只会搜到一两发子弹，且子弹面对血厚的敌人时消耗速度很快。　说到装备和武器，在《困兽》中克兰可以装备包括头部、手套、护腕、服装、运动裤、运动鞋在内的6项装备，大部分装备都可以在暗区、安全区和任务奖励中得到，并且都会带来倾向不同的效果。例如其中的“野性”套装的效果就能减少近战武器的体力消耗，并增加伤害和治疗效果，虽然集齐6件“野性”套装后并不会触发什么额外的特殊效果，但仅仅是数值上的提升就足以让玩家的生存能力强上许多了。《困兽》在武器的多样性上也迎来了一个较大的提升。
近战武器现在可以通过“模改”装上最多四个改装模组，其中尖端和柄部的模组能为武器提供传统的电击、燃烧、中毒、冰霜和冲击特效，握把和挂件模组则能够提供减少耐久度消耗、增加伤害等永久激活的被动和数值加成。　远程武器虽不能改装，却通过新增不少武器类型的方式来让玩家能玩到尽兴。
细细数来，本作大概有弓箭、弩箭、手枪、左轮、步枪、射手步枪、冲锋枪、霰弹枪、火焰喷射器、榴弹发射器、锯片发射器等不下十种的远程武器，且只要解锁，玩家就可以随时在工作台对它们进行升级与制作。
和前两作一样，本作玩家在前期弹药相对紧缺，但在中后期资源一旦累积起来，也能短暂摆脱掉弹药焦虑，带着上百发的备弹去正面硬刚BOSS。通过限制资源获取数量，提高资源消耗速率，以期让玩家在游戏的早期时刻处在资源焦虑之中，这正是Techland认为造成消光一口碑成功与消光二口碑失败的关键差异点。　此外，除了制造资源焦虑，本作对敌人的战斗力也进行了加强。
河狸谷的白天出现较多的是人类敌人和普通丧尸。
近战型的人类敌人现在不会无脑上前攻击，而是会以退为进，更倾向于在闪过或者防住玩家的攻击过后再出手;远程型的人类敌人则会优先在远处寻找掩护，并在玩家靠近时不断转移掩体。
而原本在前两代作为杂兵存在，只有数量稍多时才具备一点威胁的普通丧尸，在本作中的攻击欲望变得更强了，而且经常会以能够硬控玩家的“投技”起手，寻常攻击时也会预判玩家的位置。玩家路过尸群时，一旦离它们稍微近了一点就会被挠上几爪子，走慢了马上就会被它们扑过来抱住，等到挣脱过后转头一看，周围已经要被围得水泄不通了。当夜幕降临，夜魔也会如期而至。
这是一种运动能力极强的丧尸，堪称游戏中除了主角以外的最强战力。它们也能畅通无阻地在房顶上穿梭跑酷，不仅能跟得上克兰跑酷时的脚步，甚至偶尔还会超过主角。这种可能从任何角落发起袭击的“猎手”般的存在，让玩家时刻如履薄冰。
而主角则因为夜晚能见度极低，光源主要依赖手电筒，光影交错下，废墟和阴影中仿佛随时会冒出敌人，未知性和恐惧感油然而生。另外在夜间，感染者的低吟、嘶吼、脚步声，以及风吹过废墟的呼啸声，都极具沉浸感。紧张的背景音乐会在危险逼近时响起，进一步加剧玩家的心理压力。
从这些点就能看出，在营造“威胁感”这个方面，《困兽》确实下了一番苦功。在普通敌人和夜魔之外，《困兽》主推的“奇美拉”——男爵制造出来的强大丧尸——则是更加特殊的存在。
游戏中共存在8只奇美拉，每一只奇美拉都只有在主线剧情中才能遇见。不同的奇美拉拥有各自不同的能力，Techland从这个方面下手，设计出了多场演出和互动都颇具差异的BOSS战。　比如玩家第一个遇到的奇美拉“死神”，就是将右手的骨头当成骨刀来挥舞的近战型丧尸，其形象设计比较接近于大众印象中的死神形象，攻击方式也主要依靠挥舞骨刀。整体感受下来还算有挑战性，不过玩家也很容易就能找到应对之策。
奇美拉和大地图上会刷新的各种类型的精英丧尸不同，会使用一些新招式，而且血量更厚、体型更大、有专门的对战场地，血量下降到一定程度还会分阶段召唤小丧尸。在击败奇美拉之后，克兰可以从它们的身上提取到“GSB”并注入自己体内，然后就会获得相应的“野性点数”，也就是可供升级“野性技能”的技能点。这个分支中的技能只能在野兽模式下使用，而在点出最后一项之前——也就是游戏主线流程的中后期——玩家只能等野性之力计量条填满以后才能主动开启野兽化。　至于其他三条技能分支，由于本作的等级上限为15级，后期每升一级都会得到多个技能点，所以每一条只有7项技能，分别对应着力量、敏捷和生存，其内容十分接近前两作技能树的融合精简版。
开启野兽化后，克兰会像《消逝的光芒2》中夜魔化的艾登一样，收起手中的武器，抡圆了一双大手准备和敌人肉搏。这个状态下的克兰身体素质会得到全方位飞跃式的提升，在攻击夜魔和BOSS以外的敌人时可能会自动触发处决攻击，带来更加血型刺激的战斗场面。点出相应的技能以后，更是可以一蹦三尺高，或者违反物理定律在空中徒手直线拉钩爪，直观地演绎为什么克兰被叫做哈兰超人。对了，现在克兰所在的地方是河狸谷，应该改口叫河狸谷超人。总而言之，《消逝的光芒：困兽》是一次对系列初代精神的诚恳回归，也是一次在有限框架内的稳健拓展。
它凭借资源管控和敌群强化成功找回了生存恐怖应有的紧张与压迫，又借由河狸谷丰富精致的探索内容和人性化的任务设计，为玩家提供了张弛有度的节奏体验。尽管奇美拉BOSS战未能完全摆脱重复与套路，略显遗憾，但从暗区潜行的颤栗，到化身“河狸谷超人”横扫尸群的爽快，《困兽》依然精准地复现了那些让玩家爱上《消逝的光芒》的核心乐趣.它或许不是一场革命，但对于渴望在末日中再次感受那份挣扎与突围的玩家而言，这无疑是一场值得投入的复仇之旅。

I really enjoyed the game. Overall, it felt better than the first one, especially in gameplay, even if the story and skills were not as good.

The gameplay was just really fun. The graphics and particle effects looked great, and the gunplay was a huge improvement compared to the first game. Storms felt so immersive, and the overall atmosphere and sound effects were great. The music was also solid, with different versions of the main track from the first game. The bosses were good too, most of them looked unique and had their own mechanics. There was also a big variety of zombies. I also wasn’t sure about the Beast feature at first, but it turned out to be insane. Hahah

I bought the game because of The Restored Land update, and I’m glad I did. Fighting zombies, looting, managing hunger and flashlight battery, and driving around all felt very engaging. A true survival zombie experience, like the ones you dream as a child.

That said, there were some downsides. The most obvious one is the skill system. Many of them felt a bit boring and could have been more interesting. I also wish there was a personal truck with its own inventory. Instead, trucks just spawn and despawn randomly and don't have inventories. The legendary weapons, especially the guns, could have had more depth too, like silencers, better scopes, extended magazines, etc. Lastly, movement felt a bit slow when going sideways or backward, which was pretty annoying at times.

Overall, I really liked the game. 9/10

First of the overall game is fantastic it has some nice updated mechanics when it comes down to the battle against zombies when you are one on one with those. The gameplay and new additions are fine and all but what is up with this restored land which feels incomplete in a way when it comes to what it supposed to make you feel? You see, the second installment was a well rounded lively world build into two factions that game nuance to this franchise and make this franchise bigger than the previous installment from the second one. 

This is not what this third/dlc is at all.  2. Glitchy AI: Overall, the Volatiles are pretty buggy in the dark zones. They don't always navigate the environment naturally, I've seen them jittering or straight up teleporting instead of chasing me properly when I get to a safe area.

Dying Light: The Beast is a franchise sticking to its vision. Techland has stayed the course since the beginning, delivering the same core style of gameplay they’ve always been known for. It may not be a Game of the Year contender, but it’s still absolutely worth the time and money.
The storyline, boss fights, and weapon‑crafting system are all engaging and familiar in the best way. The game knows what it is and doesn’t pretend otherwise.
The only real criticism I have is that it might be time for a fresh framework. Reusing older assets and systems speeds up production, sure, but true creative excellence sometimes comes from starting clean - especially when you’ve learned so much over the years. A new foundation could open the door to ideas that the current engine simply can’t support.
Overall, it’s a solid entry that delivers exactly what longtime fans expect.

Dopo la grande delusione del secondo capitolo, Dying Light: The Beast è stato un po' come tornare a casa, a quelle sensazioni che mi aveva dato il capostipite della serie.
Finalmente una mappa non gigantesca con duemila icone inutili ma grande il giusto e facile da esplorare. Il Parkour la fa da padrona e con il rampino si svolazza che è una bellezza.
Ritorna il nostro amato Crane, sempre grosso ed ignorante pronto a tirare calci volanti al primo non morto che lo guarda troppo storto.
Trama semplice, un po' troppo forse alla resident-evil con un cattivo un po' macchiettistico ma che fa il suo e tirando le somme intrattiene per tutta la sua durata.
Sistema di Perk composto da quattro rami d'abilità più le abilita bestia, sempre molto semplice forse alcuni di questi potenziamenti lasciano il tempo che trovano e solo alcuni si riveleranno veramente interessanti in termini di gameplay.
Le armi bianche sono tante e molto interessanti, anche se sono presenti in quantità minore rispetto al primo capitolo e bocche da fuoco che non sono moltissime ma che sono sempre divertenti da utilizzare.
Infatti, il gore è bello deciso e gli smembramenti uniti alla fisica dei corpi daranno una soddisfazione immensa nel colpire sia gli zombie che i nemici che ci troveremo davanti.
Il sistema di guida lascia il tempo che trova ma è così marginale che per quanto brutto non inficia così tanto sull'esperienza totale.
Peccato per la nuova modalità che non si può giocare in coop (una assurdità se pensiamo di che titolo stiamo parlando) e per il fatto che non possiamo utilizzare il nostro salvataggio principale (così facendo si buttano un po' tutte le ore passate in NG+).
Questa terza iterazione per me è promossa, forse perché è più contenuta del secondo capitolo (di cui in origine doveva essere un DLC) e che diverte per tutta la sua durata senza essere tedioso con ammennicoli inutili solo per riempire il gioco di ore di gameplay spazzatura.

I hold the Dying Light series dear to me, but I cannot in good faith recommend this at full price. Not even if it's on sale.

The story was underwhelming, and despite the fact that I did 90% of the side quests, it totaled to about 28~ hours at the time of this review.
The plot was very, very cliche. And I failed to understand the Baron's at all.
The ending was also extremely mediocre.

Will delve into spoiler content about the ending here, so beware;
[spoiler]It really pisses me off that from my POV, the Baron just seems to be a psychopath madman that's drunk on his powers, speaking of, how'd he even rise to that point? The game didn't try to delve into this as much as I had hoped, and I wish they did.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]I think it's a cool reveal that at the end, Aiden, alongside Spike, were the one to rescue Kyle, but that's about the only highlight of the story for me. Spike's death was really, really unnecessary and was just used as fuel to hate the Baron even more than we already have. It was very cliche and the Baron, as a villain, didn't work for me. I did not feel satisfied to finish the story at all.[/spoiler]

Overall, this just felt really cliche, and the story didn't work for me. DL: The Beast feels more like a nostalgia trip for veterans of the previous 2 games, rather than a sequel. The gameplay part was fine for the most part, but not exactly astounding. I really wish that the parkour in this game was more incorporated into and used more. It would've helped with the repetitive fetch quests that you had to do.

The vertical spaces the map does have are horribly designed, and you end up having to stop very often to try and figure out a way up a sheer wall or across a street. Seemingly, the devs put no care into designing throughways and routes for you to parkour fluidly and effectively.

Traversing the open spaces of the map is boring, too. In The Following, you had a really cool buggy that you could customize and upgrade, as well as unlock skills in a dedicated skill tree for. You could unlock flamethrowers, boosters, an electric cage, spikes, better suspension, the whole shebang.

In The Beast, you get . . . A truck!

Can you upgrade it? No.
Can you customize it? Barely.
Is there a whole skill tree for it? 

...It has a skill for fuel consumption and a skill for durability.

That's it.

And the open world just looks bad. A lot of the map genuinely looks like what someone would make in a community map editor. The mountainous areas of the national park are particularly badly put together, and it seems like they just slapped together 2 or 3 "cliff" assets, and it is so painfully obvious that it wasn't designed with any actual realism or cohesion.

The Beast does get some things right, particularly in the QoL, but at this point it goes without saying that QoL should be good by now.

I just cannot justify this being a standalone, full priced game. Everything it does, has been done better in either DL1 or DL2. I am lucky to have gotten it for free, and with the knowledge I have after playing it, I do not recommend anyone spend full price on it. Wait until at least a 25% sale.

而困兽则没有上述的这些问题，是从DL初代通关后久违的愉快的体验。本作优化不错整体帧数稳定丝滑流畅，几乎没有遇到过什么恶性BUG也没有遇到诸如闪退之类的搞心态的问题，联机体验也相当不错裸连绝大多数时候也没什么问题（有个加速器还是最好，虽然我们裸连也并没感受到明显的延迟，但是有加速器的加持体验会更稳定）而且本作精致的僵尸建模给到很好的击杀反馈，战斗的手感也很不错，可以说本作的优秀表现让我重新喜欢上了DL系列

新的机制野兽模式可以简单理解为赛亚人怒气值够了就可以短暂的变身超赛，期间缓慢回血攻击间隔缩短且可以出发耗气的的特殊攻击。攻击普通敌人时有概率秒杀，整体是很爽的。不过这个能力是通过进攻或者挨打来积蓄充能的，且前期只能充能满了就自动变身需要等到后期有足够的技能点以后才能解锁手动释放，这个设计有点影响游戏节奏，如果想积蓄能量留着打硬仗那就只能规避很多战斗，没办法随心所欲的去战斗爽。

Not gonna lie, I bounced on Dying Light: The Beast.
Full disclosure I got this game for free (I'm honestly not sure [i]how[/i] but maybe it had to do with me also owning the Deluxe version of Dying Light 2 or something)

Let's just get on with it.
* The story? Meh. It's not engaging, a consistent problem from the 2nd game. CRANE IS BACK!... Except this time his mission is less focused and the only reason he was interesting was the fact that he was focused on a mission with conflicting priorities. I honestly can't name any of the characters.
* The parkour? Better than the second game, worse than the first. In the second game you had to spam C while jumping over literally any object to get slight speed boosts, here you just don't do that which makes it less annoying. Similarly movement is more like the first as I haven't gotten any gimmicks like the glider or grappling hook which, if both are missing, [b]good.[/b]
* Combat? Boring, repetitive, etc. Played part of this game on harder difficulties and it's just not fun in the slightest as every enemy is a sponge so I hope you're ready to soak multiple weapons into bosses! Normal and under the game is far easier but you'll still die due to the routine garbage that is this game's tendency of just having a ton of zombies hiding in corners waiting patiently to be annoying.
* Night time? Pretty bad. Large sections of the map are open so volatiles will see you easily so you'll constantly be in chase, and they are still just as deadly as always making getting caught out unfun.
* RPG mechanics maintain being garbage. This time the game locks several QOL specific upgrades behind several levels and boss kills which leads me into my next rant:
* The titular Beast Mode for Crane is [b]hoooorrreeeeennnnddddooooouuuuussssss[/b] and I can't state that loud enough. When you deal damage or take damage you build your Beast meter, and when it's full you are forced to unleash the Beast! If you've [i]ever played any game where you can go #beastmode on enemies you will know why this sucks already.[/i] For those who haven't: You don't really control when you go Beast mode, making it equal parts extremely strong and literally useless which is terrible for the [b]one[/b] innovation to the Dying Light formula that is here. Now you can buy the unlock to control when Beast Mode activates... After you kill [b]3 bosses[/b] which is exceptionally annoying. It's worth noting that it can't be just [i]any[/i] boss enemy, it explicitly has to be a boss for a story mode mission and these all are actual garbage! The first boss is a Charger enemy that you'll fight out in the wild, just bigger. The second is a leaping Hunter style enemy who will leap at you before scurrying away to try again and I can't even tell you what the 3rd one is cause I bounced. I can't express enough how absolutely [i]garbage[/i] it is to constantly activate #BeastMode on the final enemy of a horde because you [b]DARED[/b] to have fun and explore the game world, how annoying it is that during Beast Mode you can't heal so if you activate while already low on health you are an easy target for any enemy to kill. It's not all downsides though: Your punches heal you and you deal increased damage!... Which is again only useful if [i]you, the player[/i] get to decide when it happens, not the game, and that isn't how it is by default and having to buy a standard feature for this type of thing in a game is never good design as far as I'm concerned.
* UI is intensely bad and is made for console players pretty exclusively. Navigating it with Mouse + Keyboard is awful. Do you want to repair a weapon? You have two options: 1) Hold down the 3 button with your second finger that you have on W, then use your mouse to hover over the weapon, then hold the R key with your first finger to repair the weapon. Or 2) Open your inventory, wait 4 or 5 seconds for things to load in, find the weapon and click on [b]IT SPECIFICALLY THIS IS IMPORTANT[/b] then repair it, exit which takes a few seconds, and continue fighting. [i]Every single time a weapon breaks you will have to do this. You will be doing this in the middle of combat, you will be doing this while exploring, you will always be doing this. It is really, really, really garbage. I do not have words for how much I hated doing this after having to kill a single horde of zombies because, again, I had the gall to go exploring.[/i] During my Dying Light 2 review I said that Techland really has to pick a lane between either being a combat focused game where weapons don't break or being Breath of the Wild with Zombies and somehow The Beast kept the bad decisions from 2 (OP weapons if you craft them) while making durability far more of an issue. If there is a mod that disables weapon breaking, the game's economy might break but at least you can have some fun. This is just a microcosm of how bad the UI is, many other examples exist! The map, while flashy and cool, is unhelpful at best. The journal + quest log sucks. Equipping and unequipping items sucks. Everything is clearly made to be played with a controller in hand to such an extent that I don't even know why they bothered to include a Mouse + KB option.
* EDIT: I didn't mention the trucks but they... [i]Exist[/i] I guess. Not nearly as noteworthy as they were in The Following, still a massive downgrade in every way, control like garbage and they have limited fuel which adds yet another annoying chore to Dying Light: The Beast: Annoying Chores Land Edition.
* Restored Land is the biggest shrug I could ever give to anything ever. I have no clue why it exists and I don't think it adds anything to the game on any level.
* Stretched to give the game something positive, it has a very pretty sandbox for you to run around in, it's just very shallow.

There just isn't enough here and the pain points from prior in the series are not only still here but they are even worse than they were back then. This is definitely going to be my last Dying Light game, cause oh my goodness I'm really tired of this ride and [i]I want off.[/i]

一代始發就入坑的老倉鼠玩家

1.遊戲整體規模
一代和二代都玩了130小時左右
困獸真的是DLC改來的作品，噩夢難度主線慢慢玩大概50小時第一輪主支線+暗區&安全屋全開
不得不說整體來說短了不少，但我個人是很滿足的，短小精悍且內容充實。
對於已經開始邁入中年的我而言，剛好在最完美的時間結束，這點我給予很高的評價，
遊戲不是脫台錢就好的，很多遊戲玩到後面就只是追求破關痛苦的玩著，困獸剛好在膩之前的甜蜜點結束。
很推薦一開始就用噩夢難度遊玩，恰到好處的資源限制和敵人強度，不會因為太簡單而感到乏味。
破關後感覺其實可以直接用夢魘模式，如此一來體驗更佳刺激。

2.地圖&跑酷
雖然跟二代比起來地圖小了很多，但明顯整體的精緻度比二代高，
跑酷起來的舒適度也比二代好很多，希望新的三代也能維持這種小而美且精緻的地圖製造模式。

3.跳臉驚嚇&戰鬥
各種門後和角落的敵人配置真的不是很友好...
也許喜歡跳臉驚嚇的玩家很多? 我只是個玩家所以我只能說我真的很不喜歡這味(一代跟二代我記得也沒有...)
戰鬥方面
普通感染者全體擒拿術達人且範圍很長，的確一開始玩很有壓迫感沒錯，但新鮮度過去後就只覺得非常令人煩躁而已...
夜魔的強度提升，2代的夜魔真的太弱了，沒有壓迫感... 困獸裡跟夜魔纏鬥真的是血脈噴張心跳狂飆，很棒。

4.劇情&人物塑造
很高興這代的人物都很正常，至少沒有二代的拉萬....
劇情任務跟整體描寫都很棒，沒有將軍十松莊的馬桶又塞了那種無意義的支線，每個支線都很有趣。(除了賽車支線...)

5.優化
50個小時的遊玩目前沒有遇到任何BUG和閃退
NV用自動最佳化設定個人感覺很流暢沒有明顯卡頓。

結語
跑酷&喪屍也僅此一家，且玩且珍惜。
這年頭不犯大錯就可惜可賀的年代個人很推薦困獸的，
但不推薦新玩家直接從困獸開始入坑此系列，
當然從1代開始最好，但畢竟是10年前的老作品了，畫面和遊戲性都有點過時，
建議從2代開始玩，對胃口再去補完1代最後再玩困獸，
1代的劇情在困獸裡有很重的描寫，至少我個人是很受感觸的。

Хороша ностальгія.
Я хотів почекати десь рік, а потім купити десь за 800 грн, але не витримав та купив за 1200 (і це зі знижкою), бо зловив жорсткий гіперфікс на волохатих цицьках Кайла Крейна.

Графіка. Вона хороша. Не шедевральна — просто хороша. Про якість текстур нічого не скажу, бо я не графодрочер, та загальна атмосфера, ландшафт і кольорова палітра дуже приємні. Я не сумую за жовтизною Харану чи цвітастістю Вілідору. Тут просто гарно. На диво, з моєю збіркою ПК нерідко ловив вильоти. Грав десь на передмаксимальних — гра працювала стабільно, без тормозів, але просто вилітала на початку сюжетки.

Паркур. В DL1 він був «реалістичним», як деякі кажуть, але я б радше назвав його «приземленим» та дещо топорним, без особливого мувменту. Коротше, непоганий скетч, який треба було правити. В DL2 все підправили. Рухів більше, персонаж жвавіший — майже як Mirror’s Edge Catalyst, але ще краще: з паропланом, фізично правильним крюком та елементами «павер-фентезі». До речі, вважаю, що гравцю замість пароплану варто було давати крюк, бо занадто вже легко паркурити та тікати на початку гри. Так що ж по DL Beast? Рухи та анімації дуже подібні до DL2, але все трохи сповільнено та зроблено важчим. Іншими словами, стало більш заземлено. Місто по паркуру відчувається ніби «Старе місто» із DL1, але з невеличкими наворотами DL2.

Складність у мене була «Brutal», і це реально відчувалося як виживання. Зброї на початку мало, вона швидко ламається, набоїв небагато, але й ті не дуже ефективні проти зомбі. Ночі — реально можна обісратися. Який би кут зору ви не поставили, видима ділянка у вас — тільки кружечок ліхтарика. Ніби ти проходиш гру в кружечку Telegram. Які б відео ви не дивилися, знайте: вживу ти нічого не бачиш по боках. Та по ходу сюжету ви стаєте вправнішими, трохи спритнішими, проте дуже потужними. Режим Біста прикольний, але я його використовував тільки на босах або коли не вивозив солдатиків. Спробую якось побігати з ним по місту.

Сюжет. Він… простенький. Якийсь нарцисичний соціопат-вчений, який, типу, все спланував: він такий розумний, а всі — маріонетки… Але він не такий придуркувато-ідіотський, як у DL2. Діалоги реалістичні. Я вірю в те, як люди тут спілкуються. Кайл, як родзинка, постійно коментує свою ситуацію та положення, що розряджає напругу: «Вирвався з пекла, щоб працювати сантехніком». Моя англійська, якщо чесно, херовенька, але сюжет загалом зрозумів. На жаль, український текст ще не завезли, а фанатська локалізація лише нещодавно додалася для DL2. Зате русні дісталася повна локалізація. Поляки з Techland тут трохи зрадоньку зробили, на відміну від CD Projekt Red у Cyberpunk 2077 із хорошою текстовою локалізацією та припиненням голосової локалізації для Phantom Liberty.

Саундтрек приємний. Трохи однотипний, бо використовує за основу один трек із DL1, але акустичну гітару можна слухати довго — пробачаю.

Загалом не шкодую про її купівлю. Та вона відчувається короткою, і хочеться ще.

DL: The Beast feels like a weak spin-off that somehow made everything worse. Like even worse than DL2's downgrades. Crane is supposed to be a juiced hybrid now but all the zombies are incredibly sturdy and all being juiced does is give you a very short hulk mode that you can't even control when it activates until many hours in. And who thought it was a good idea to put search, finishing move, and grapple toss all on the same button? I had to get a mod to make it so I search without the hold button delay it was so obnoxious. There's a bunch of other small annoyances like the dash mode not deciding if it's on or not so you can't tell if you're doing to do the running bash move. Just get Dying Light 1 with the expansion insead.
